theorems.conclusion: sum_(x in F_p) e_p(d*x) equals p if d=0 and 0 otherwise; 1_(z=t)=p^(-1)*sum_r e_p(r*(z-t)).

theorems.title: Rectangular bilinear character bound
hypotheses: A and B are nonempty subsets of F_p
r is a nonzero element of F_p
X and Y are independent, uniform on A and B
theorems.conclusion: |sum_(a in A,b in B) e_p(r*a*b)| <= sqrt(p*|A|*|B|), and |E[e_p(r*X*Y)]| <= sqrt(p/(|A||B|)); independently, |E[e_p(r*X*Y)]| <= 1.

theorems.title: Independent-sum Fourier mixing
hypotheses: beta_i >= 0 and |E[e_p(r*U_i)]| <= beta_i for every r != 0
theorems.conclusion: For every t, |Pr(sum_i U_i=t)-1/p| <= ((p-1)/p)*product_i beta_i. If (p-1)*product_i beta_i < 1, every residue has positive probability.

theorems.title: Heterogeneous rectangular product sums
hypotheses: A_i and B_i are nonempty subsets of F_p
All coordinate samples X_i in A_i and Y_i in B_i are independent and uniform
c_i is nonzero in F_p for each i; d is in F_p
theorems.conclusion: For Z=d+sum_i c_i*X_i*Y_i and every t, |Pr(Z=t)-1/p| <= ((p-1)/p)*sqrt(p^k/M). If M>(p-1)^2*p^k, every residue occurs.

theorems.title: General k-product covering criterion
hypotheses: A and B are nonempty subsets of F_p
theorems.conclusion: Every t in F_p is sum_(i=1..k) a_i*b_i with a_i in A,b_i in B. For A=B=H, the criterion is (p-1)*(sqrt(p)/|H|)^k < 1.

theorems.title: Radical-free representation-count inequality
hypotheses: All hypotheses of FF005 except its optional strict size condition
C_t is the number of tuples whose weighted sum plus shift equals t
theorems.conclusion: sum_t C_t=M and (p*C_t-M)^2 <= (p-1)^2*p^k*M. If M>(p-1)^2*p^k, then C_t>=1 for every t.

theorems.title: Four products cover at three-quarter density
hypotheses: A,B are nonempty subsets of F_p
Four factor pairs are independent and uniform
theorems.conclusion: For every t, Pr(sum_(i=1..4) X_i*Y_i=t) >= [1-(p-1)*p^2/N^2]/p >= 1/p^2, and C_t>=N^4/p^2. In particular it holds for A=B=H with |H|>=p^(3/4).

theorems.title: Lift a zero product-sum to positive rational divisors
hypotheses: D is a nonempty set of positive divisors of Q
H is the image of D modulo p
x_i,y_i in H and sum_i x_i*y_i=0 in F_p
theorems.conclusion: Choose positive representatives a_i,b_i in D and e_i=a_i*b_i. Then e_i divides Q^2, t=(sum_i e_i)/p is a positive integer, and p=sum_i e_i/t.

theorems.title: Local four-summand prime lift
theorems.conclusion: The prime p has a representation p=sum_(i=1..4) e_i/t with positive e_i dividing Q^2 and a common positive integer t.
